introduction: From the Space Shuttle, aurora appears as a luminous layer suspended above Earth’s dark horizon.
observe: Separate the curved horizon from the glow above it.
Look for structure within the luminous band rather than on the surface.
explanation: The STS-45 crew photographed the aurora australis from orbit. Aurora is produced high in an atmosphere when energetic particles interact with gases along a planet’s magnetic environment.
colorMethod: This photographic view records visible emission from atmospheric gases, shaped by exposure and viewing conditions.
whyItMatters: Aurora links a visible atmospheric event to an otherwise invisible magnetic interaction.
